correctness.rationale: PASS: At alpha beta=1, the Zak-fiber norm reduces (up to 2pi/alpha) to the modulus of sum_j a_j r_j^t/(1-r_j z), with 0<t<1, |z|=1, and r_j=e^{-2pi w_j/alpha}. The positive-residue real-part bound gives lower L=sum a_j r_j/(1+r_j); the triangle bound gives upper U=sum a_j/(1-r_j). Both extrema are essential limits at z=-1,t=1 and z=1,t=0. Hence exact squared frame bounds are 4pi²L²/alpha and 4pi²U²/alpha, not merely admissible estimates. With q_j=(a_j r_j/(1+r_j))/L, U/L=sum q_j (1+r_j)/(r_j(1-r_j)); exact factorization at r*=sqrt2-1 yields B/A=(1+sqrt2)^4(1+D)^2 and strict equality classification. At delta>0, r(1-r)<=1/4 implies q-mass outside delta <=D/(4delta²). This is an analytical infinite-parameter proof; finite script examples do not establish it.
